rows.question: anything to destress b4 finals week
rows.answer:
**General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): Try a short walk, a few minutes of slow breathing, and a regular bedtime. Break studying into small blocks with brief breaks, and focus on the next manageable task rather than the whole week. Make time for water, meals, and something relaxing you enjoy.

Yes. The Center for Reading and Writing is offering a free 45-minute “Study Skills to Survive the End of the Semester” workshop online on November 23, 2026, from 1:15 to 2:00 p.m. It covers reading, annotating, and recall strategies, time management, taking care of your health, and campus resources. All students are welcome. Register: [https://cglink.me/2fF/r1409516](https://cglink.me/2fF/r1409516). For more information, contact Priscilla Tovey at ptovey@ramapo.edu. [12]

For a quick check-in, Counseling Services has a free, anonymous mental health screening to help identify areas of distress: [https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/mental-health-screening/](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/mental-health-screening/) [18]

- **Center for Reading and Writing**: Phone: (201) 684-7557. Email: crw@ramapo.edu. Location: Peter P. Mercer Learning Commons, Room 420. Outreach Coordinator: LC-424; Developmental Writing Specialist: LC-425; Reading Specialist: LC-423. [34]

rows.question: anything for destressing the next couple days? need a break bad
rows.answer:
Sorry to hear that!

**General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): For the next couple of days, keep things simple: take a short walk, get regular sleep, eat and drink normally, and set aside a little time for something relaxing. Try a few minutes of slow breathing—breathe in gently, then make your exhale a bit longer. If you can, write down what’s weighing on you and choose one small next step; let non-urgent tasks wait.

The Wellness Room (E-216) has yoga mats, a light therapy lamp, a weighted blanket, a massage chair, coloring activities, and stress-reduction pamphlets. Reserve a time, then pick up the key from the Center for Student Involvement. [19][29]

You could also try mindfulness, journaling, or reflecting on small wins. [18]

There’s a meditation tonight, Wednesday, November 18, from 7–7:30 pm in the Wellness Room (E-216); RSVP on Archway: [https://cglink.me/2fF/r1410364](https://cglink.me/2fF/r1410364). [20]
